target.rawSql: SELECT period_start AS time, 'anomaly' AS text, CASE WHEN forest_flagged THEN 'forest' ELSE 'flatline' END AS tags FROM pjm_lmp_anomalies WHERE zone='$zone' AND (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND $__timeFilter(period_start)

targets.rawSql: SELECT lmp_price AS value FROM pjm_lmp_readings WHERE zone='$zone' AND quality != 'missing' ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT max(lmp_price) AS value FROM pjm_lmp_readings WHERE zone='$zone' AND period_start > now() - interval '24 hours'

panels.title: Data freshness ($zone)
panels.description: Time since the most recent LMP reading for this zone. The live feed posts every 5 minutes, so a healthy value here is well under 10 minutes.

targets.rawSql: SELECT extract(epoch from (now() - max(period_start))) AS value FROM pjm_lmp_readings WHERE zone='$zone'
SELECT count(*) AS value FROM pjm_lmp_anomalies WHERE zone='$zone' AND (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND scored_at > now() - interval '7 days'

panels.title: All 5 zones, anomalies flagged (7d)
panels.description: Cross-zone view, independent of the $zone selector above, so a stress event isolated to one zone is still visible from this panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT zone AS "Zone", count(*) AS "Anomalies (7d)" FROM pjm_lmp_anomalies WHERE (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND scored_at > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY zone ORDER BY zone

panels.title: LMP vs forecast ($zone)
panels.description: Forecast is the seasonal-naive baseline the detector scores against (7-day lag at 5-minute grain), derived as actual - residual, not a separately stored column.

targets.rawSql: SELECT r.period_start AS time, r.lmp_price AS actual, (r.lmp_price - a.residual) AS forecast FROM pjm_lmp_readings r LEFT JOIN pjm_lmp_anomalies a ON a.period_start = r.period_start AND a.zone = r.zone WHERE r.zone='$zone' AND $__timeFilter(r.period_start) ORDER BY r.period_start

panels.title: Forecast residuals ($zone)
panels.description: The series the isolation forest actually scores. Flagged points are overlaid separately so you can see why something was flagged.

targets.rawSql: SELECT period_start AS time, residual, CASE WHEN forest_flagged THEN residual ELSE NULL END AS flagged FROM pjm_lmp_anomalies WHERE zone='$zone' AND $__timeFilter(period_start) ORDER BY period_start

SELECT period_start AS "Time", residual AS "Residual ($/MWh)", forest_score AS "Forest score", forest_flagged AS "Forest flagged", flatline_flagged AS "Flatline flagged", scored_at AS "Scored at" FROM pjm_lmp_anomalies WHERE zone='$zone' AND (forest_flagged OR flatline_flagged) AND $__timeFilter(period_start) ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 100

options.content: **How this detector works.** Same method as the public dashboard: an isolation forest on forecast residuals plus rolling context, fit per zone on a time-based train/validation split, with a separate rule-based flatline check running alongside it. No real anomaly labels exist for this data; detector quality is measured via synthetic-anomaly injection on held-out data, a check on the method, not a guarantee about real events. **Data-center interconnection correlation is not shown here.** It was planned as a core feature but is confirmed deferred (ARCHITECTURE.md Section 3): PJM's Large Load Registry took effect 2026-10-12 and public access, once defined, will be aggregated-only; PJM's own compliance filing describing the actual access mechanism is not due until around 2026-11-08. There is nothing to correlate against yet. This dashboard and its underlying data are PJM Data Miner 2 sourced and are never exposed on the public dashboard or any externally shared link, per PJM's non-member redistribution terms.
